title: Two Sum
question: Find two array indices whose elements sum up to a target value.
explanation: We iterate through the array while maintaining a hash map of numbers seen so far and their indices. For each number, we check if target - current number exists in the map. If found, we return both indices. This resolves the problem in a single pass with O(n) time and O(n) space.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION twoSum(nums, target):
    map = EMPTY_HASH_MAP()
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        complement = target - nums[i]
        IF complement IN map THEN RETURN [map[complement], i]
        map[nums[i]] = i
    END FOR
    RETURN []
END FUNCTION

title: Add Two Numbers
question: Add two numbers represented by reversed linked lists and return the sum as a linked list.
explanation: We traverse both linked lists node by node, summing corresponding digits along with any carry from the previous position. We create new nodes for the ones digit of each sum and propagate the carry to the next iteration, effectively simulating column-by-column addition in O(max(N, M)) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION addTwoNumbers(l1, l2):
    dummy = NEW Node(0), curr = dummy, carry = 0
    WHILE l1 OR l2 OR carry DO:
        val1 = l1 ? l1.val : 0
        val2 = l2 ? l2.val : 0
        sum = val1 + val2 + carry
        carry = sum / 10
        curr.next = NEW Node(sum % 10)
        curr = curr.next
        IF l1 THEN l1 = l1.next
        IF l2 THEN l2 = l2.next
    END WHILE
    RETURN dummy.next
END FUNCTION

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
question: Find the length of the longest substring containing no duplicate characters.
explanation: We use a sliding window approach maintained by two pointers (left and right) along with a set of visited characters. As the right pointer expands the window, if a duplicate is found, the left pointer shrinks the window from the left until all characters inside the window are unique again.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION lengthOfLongestSubstring(s):
    charSet = EMPTY_SET(), left = 0, maxLength = 0
    FOR right FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        WHILE s[right] IN charSet DO:
            REMOVE s[left] FROM charSet
            left = left + 1
        END WHILE
        ADD s[right] TO charSet
        maxLength = MAX(maxLength, right - left + 1)
    END FOR
    RETURN maxLength
END FUNCTION

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
question: Find the median of two sorted arrays in logarithmic time complexity.
explanation: We apply binary search on the smaller of the two sorted arrays to partition both arrays into equal left and right halves. We adjust the binary search range until all elements in the left partition are less than or equal to all elements in the right partition, yielding O(log(min(m, n))) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findMedianSortedArrays(nums1, nums2):
    IF LENGTH(nums1) > LENGTH(nums2) THEN RETURN findMedianSortedArrays(nums2, nums1)
    m = LENGTH(nums1), n = LENGTH(nums2), low = 0, high = m
    WHILE low <= high DO:
        i = (low + high) / 2, j = (m + n + 1) / 2 - i
        maxLeft1 = (i == 0) ? -INF : nums1[i-1]
        minRight1 = (i == m) ? INF : nums1[i]
        maxLeft2 = (j == 0) ? -INF : nums2[j-1]
        minRight2 = (j == n) ? INF : nums2[j]
        IF maxLeft1 <= minRight2 AND maxLeft2 <= minRight1 THEN:
            IF (m + n) % 2 == 0 THEN RETURN (MAX(maxLeft1, maxLeft2) + MIN(minRight1, minRight2)) / 2.0
            ELSE RETURN MAX(maxLeft1, maxLeft2)
        ELSE IF maxLeft1 > minRight2 THEN high = i - 1
        ELSE low = i + 1
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
question: Find the longest substring in a given string that reads the same backward as forward.
explanation: Every palindrome centers around either a single character (odd length) or two adjacent equal characters (even length). We iterate through each index of the string, treating it as the center, and expand outward as long as the surrounding characters match.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION longestPalindrome(s):
    res = ''
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        p1 = expandAroundCenter(s, i, i)
        p2 = expandAroundCenter(s, i, i + 1)
        IF LENGTH(p1) > LENGTH(res) THEN res = p1
        IF LENGTH(p2) > LENGTH(res) THEN res = p2
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION expandAroundCenter(s, l, r):
    WHILE l >= 0 AND r < LENGTH(s) AND s[l] == s[r] DO:
        l = l - 1, r = r + 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN SUBSTRING(s, l + 1, r)
END FUNCTION

title: Container With Most Water
question: Find two vertical lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding maximum water.
explanation: We place pointers at both ends of the array. The area is constrained by the shorter line, so at each step we calculate the current container volume and then move the pointer pointing to the shorter height inward, attempting to find a taller boundary.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxArea(height):
    left = 0, right = LENGTH(height) - 1, maxW = 0
    WHILE left < right DO:
        area = (right - left) * MIN(height[left], height[right])
        maxW = MAX(maxW, area)
        IF height[left] < height[right] THEN left = left + 1
        ELSE right = right - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN maxW
END FUNCTION

title: 3Sum
question: Find all unique triplets in an array that sum to zero.
explanation: First sort the array to handle duplicates easily. Iterate through each element as a fixed target, then use a two-pointer approach on the remaining right portion of the array to find pairs that sum to the negated target value.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION threeSum(nums):
    SORT(nums), res = []
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 3 DO:
        IF i > 0 AND nums[i] == nums[i-1] THEN CONTINUE
        l = i + 1, r = LENGTH(nums) - 1
        WHILE l < r DO:
            sum = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
            IF sum == 0 THEN:
                APPEND [nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]] TO res
                WHILE l < r AND nums[l] == nums[l+1] DO l = l + 1
                WHILE l < r AND nums[r] == nums[r-1] DO r = r - 1
                l = l + 1, r = r - 1
            ELSE IF sum < 0 THEN l = l + 1
            ELSE r = r - 1
        END WHILE
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
question: Return all possible letter combinations that a digit string could represent on a phone keypad.
explanation: Using backtracking (depth-first search), we process the string digit by digit. For each digit, we loop through all corresponding characters mapped on a phone keypad and recurse to construct all valid decision path combinations.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION letterCombinations(digits):
    IF digits IS EMPTY THEN RETURN []
    map = {'2':'abc', '3':'def', '4':'ghi', '5':'jkl', '6':'mno', '7':'pqrs', '8':'tuv', '9':'wxyz'}
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(index, currentStr):
        IF index == LENGTH(digits) THEN APPEND currentStr TO res; RETURN
        FOR char IN map[digits[index]] DO:
            backtrack(index + 1, currentStr + char)
        END FOR
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0, '')
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
question: Remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list in a single pass.
explanation: We use two pointers separated by n steps. When the fast pointer reaches the end of the list, the slow pointer will be positioned right before the target node, allowing us to bypass it in O(1) extra space and O(N) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION removeNthFromEnd(head, n):
    dummy = NEW Node(0, head), fast = dummy, slow = dummy
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n DO fast = fast.next
    WHILE fast IS NOT NULL DO:
        fast = fast.next, slow = slow.next
    END WHILE
    slow.next = slow.next.next
    RETURN dummy.next
END FUNCTION

title: Valid Parentheses
question: Determine if an input string of brackets has correct opening and closing order.
explanation: We push opening brackets onto a stack. When encountering a closing bracket, we check if it matches the top element of the stack. If it matches, we pop it; otherwise, or if the stack is empty, the string is invalid.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isValid(s):
    stack = EMPTY_STACK()
    bracketMap = {')': '(', '}': '{', ']': '['}
    FOR char IN s DO:
        IF char IN bracketMap.values() THEN PUSH char TO stack
        ELSE IF char IN bracketMap.keys() THEN:
            IF stack IS EMPTY OR TOP(stack) != bracketMap[char] THEN RETURN False
            POP stack
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN IS_EMPTY(stack)
END FUNCTION

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
question: Merge two sorted linked lists into one single sorted list.
explanation: We compare the current nodes of both lists using a dummy starting node. We attach the smaller node to the merged list and advance its pointer until one list is exhausted, then append the remaining nodes.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION mergeTwoLists(l1, l2):
    dummy = NEW Node(0), curr = dummy
    WHILE l1 IS NOT NULL AND l2 IS NOT NULL DO:
        IF l1.val <= l2.val THEN curr.next = l1; l1 = l1.next
        ELSE curr.next = l2; l2 = l2.next
        curr = curr.next
    END WHILE
    curr.next = l1 ? l1 : l2
    RETURN dummy.next
END FUNCTION

title: Generate Parentheses
question: Generate all combinations of n pairs of well-formed parentheses.
explanation: We build valid strings recursively using backtracking. An open parenthesis can be added if the count is under n, and a closing parenthesis can only be added if it does not exceed the count of currently open parentheses.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION generateParenthesis(n):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(openCount, closeCount, current):
        IF LENGTH(current) == 2 * n THEN APPEND current TO res; RETURN
        IF openCount < n THEN backtrack(openCount + 1, closeCount, current + '(')
        IF closeCount < openCount THEN backtrack(openCount, closeCount + 1, current + ')')
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0, 0, '')
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
question: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list efficiently.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION mergeKLists(lists):
    minHeap = NEW MinHeap()
    FOR EACH list IN lists DO:
        IF list IS NOT NULL THEN minHeap.PUSH(list)
    END FOR
    dummy = NEW Node(0), curr = dummy
    WHILE minHeap IS NOT EMPTY DO:
        node = minHeap.POP()
        curr.next = node
        curr = curr.next
        IF node.next IS NOT NULL THEN minHeap.PUSH(node.next)
    END WHILE
    RETURN dummy.next
END FUNCTION
explanation: We insert the head node of each of the k linked lists into a min-heap. We repeatedly extract the smallest node from the min-heap, append it to our result list, and push its next node into the heap, achieving O(N log k) time.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
question: Search for a target value in a sorted array that has been rotated at an unknown pivot.
explanation: In a rotated sorted array, at least one half (left or right) is guaranteed to be strictly sorted at any step. Using modified binary search, we determine which half is sorted and check if the target falls within its range to eliminate half the search space.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION search(nums, target):
    low = 0, high = LENGTH(nums) - 1
    WHILE low <= high DO:
        mid = (low + high) / 2
        IF nums[mid] == target THEN RETURN mid
        IF nums[low] <= nums[mid] THEN:
            IF nums[low] <= target AND target < nums[mid] THEN high = mid - 1
            ELSE low = mid + 1
        ELSE:
            IF nums[mid] < target AND target <= nums[high] THEN low = mid + 1
            ELSE high = mid - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN -1
END FUNCTION

title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
question: Find the starting and ending index of a given target value in a sorted array.
explanation: We execute binary search twice: once configured to continue searching left upon finding target to record the leftmost index, and once configured to continue searching right to record the rightmost index.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION searchRange(nums, target):
    first = findBound(nums, target, True)
    IF first == -1 THEN RETURN [-1, -1]
    last = findBound(nums, target, False)
    RETURN [first, last]
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION findBound(nums, target, isFirst):
    low = 0, high = LENGTH(nums) - 1, idx = -1
    WHILE low <= high DO:
        mid = (low + high) / 2
        IF nums[mid] == target THEN:
            idx = mid
            IF isFirst THEN high = mid - 1 ELSE low = mid + 1
        ELSE IF nums[mid] < target THEN low = mid + 1
        ELSE high = mid - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN idx
END FUNCTION

title: Combination Sum
question: Find all unique combinations of candidate numbers that sum up to a target with unlimited reuse allowed.
explanation: Using depth-first search with backtracking, we explore paths where each candidate can be reused repeatedly until the current running sum equals or exceeds the target.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION combinationSum(candidates, target):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(idx, current, sum):
        IF sum == target THEN APPEND COPY(current) TO res; RETURN
        IF sum > target OR idx >= LENGTH(candidates) THEN RETURN
        APPEND candidates[idx] TO current
        backtrack(idx, current, sum + candidates[idx])
        POP current
        backtrack(idx + 1, current, sum)
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0, [], 0)
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Trapping Rain Water
question: Calculate how much rainwater an elevation map can trap after raining.
explanation: We maintain two pointers (left and right) and track leftMax and rightMax values. The trapped water over any bar is dictated by min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[i], allowing us to calculate total trapped water in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION trap(height):
    l = 0, r = LENGTH(height) - 1, leftMax = 0, rightMax = 0, water = 0
    WHILE l < r DO:
        IF height[l] < height[r] THEN:
            IF height[l] >= leftMax THEN leftMax = height[l]
            ELSE water = water + (leftMax - height[l])
            l = l + 1
        ELSE:
            IF height[r] >= rightMax THEN rightMax = height[r]
            ELSE water = water + (rightMax - height[r])
            r = r - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN water
END FUNCTION

title: Permutations
question: Return all possible permutations of an array of distinct integers.
explanation: Using backtracking, we iteratively swap the current element with all subsequent positions to systematically construct every distinct arrangement of elements in O(N!) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION permute(nums):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(start):
        IF start == LENGTH(nums) THEN APPEND COPY(nums) TO res; RETURN
        FOR i FROM start TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
            SWAP(nums[start], nums[i])
            backtrack(start + 1)
            SWAP(nums[start], nums[i])
        END FOR
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0)
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Rotate Image
question: Rotate an n x n 2D matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
explanation: A 90-degree clockwise rotation is mathematically equivalent to transposing the matrix (swapping rows with columns across the main diagonal) and then reversing every individual row.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION rotate(matrix):
    n = LENGTH(matrix)
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1 DO:
        FOR j FROM i TO n - 1 DO:
            SWAP(matrix[i][j], matrix[j][i])
        END FOR
    END FOR
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1 DO:
        REVERSE(matrix[i])
    END FOR
END FUNCTION

title: Group Anagrams
question: Group an array of strings together if they are anagrams of each other.
explanation: Since anagrams have identical character counts, sorting the string alphabetically yields a canonical key. We map this sorted key to a list of original words in a hash map.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION groupAnagrams(strs):
    map = EMPTY_HASH_MAP()
    FOR str IN strs DO:
        key = SORT_CHARACTERS(str)
        IF key NOT IN map THEN map[key] = []
        APPEND str TO map[key]
    END FOR
    RETURN VALUES(map)
END FUNCTION

title: N-Queens
question: Place n queens on an n x n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other.
explanation: We place queens row by row using backtracking while tracking occupied columns and positive/negative diagonals using hash sets to prevent conflicting placements.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION solveNQueens(n):
    res = [], cols = SET(), posDiag = SET(), negDiag = SET(), board = MATRIX(n, n, '.')
    FUNCTION backtrack(r):
        IF r == n THEN APPEND FORMAT(board) TO res; RETURN
        FOR c FROM 0 TO n - 1 DO:
            IF c IN cols OR (r+c) IN posDiag OR (r-c) IN negDiag THEN CONTINUE
            ADD c TO cols, ADD r+c TO posDiag, ADD r-c TO negDiag
            board[r][c] = 'Q'
            backtrack(r + 1)
            REMOVE c FROM cols, REMOVE r+c FROM posDiag, REMOVE r-c FROM negDiag
            board[r][c] = '.'
        END FOR
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0)
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Maximum Subarray
question: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum.
explanation: Using Kadane's algorithm, we iterate through the array maintaining a running maximum sum. If the sum drops below zero, we reset it to zero since a negative sum cannot contribute to a larger future subarray.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxSubArray(nums):
    maxSum = nums[0], currSum = nums[0]
    FOR i FROM 1 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        currSum = MAX(nums[i], currSum + nums[i])
        maxSum = MAX(maxSum, currSum)
    END FOR
    RETURN maxSum
END FUNCTION

title: Spiral Matrix
question: Return all elements of an m x n matrix in spiral order.
explanation: We maintain four boundaries: top, bottom, left, and right. We traverse along the top boundary, right boundary, bottom boundary, and left boundary sequentially while shrinking boundaries inward until all elements are collected.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION spiralOrder(matrix):
    top = 0, bottom = LENGTH(matrix) - 1, left = 0, right = LENGTH(matrix[0]) - 1, res = []
    WHILE top <= bottom AND left <= right DO:
        FOR i FROM left TO right DO APPEND matrix[top][i] TO res
        top = top + 1
        FOR i FROM top TO bottom DO APPEND matrix[i][right] TO res
        right = right - 1
        IF top <= bottom THEN
            FOR i FROM right DOWN TO left DO APPEND matrix[bottom][i] TO res
            bottom = bottom - 1
        END IF
        IF left <= right THEN
            FOR i FROM bottom DOWN TO top DO APPEND matrix[i][left] TO res
            left = left + 1
        END IF
    END WHILE
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Jump Game
question: Determine if you can reach the last index of an array given maximum jump lengths.
explanation: Using a greedy approach, we track the furthest reachable index as we traverse the array. If our current index ever exceeds this maximum reachable index, reaching the end is impossible.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION canJump(nums):
    maxReach = 0
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        IF i > maxReach THEN RETURN False
        maxReach = MAX(maxReach, i + nums[i])
    END FOR
    RETURN True
END FUNCTION

title: Merge Intervals
question: Merge all overlapping intervals in an array.
explanation: Sort intervals by their start times. Iterate through them, merging adjacent intervals whenever the current interval's start time is less than or equal to the previous interval's end time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION merge(intervals):
    SORT(intervals BY start_time), merged = []
    FOR interval IN intervals DO:
        IF merged IS EMPTY OR LAST(merged).end < interval.start THEN APPEND interval TO merged
        ELSE LAST(merged).end = MAX(LAST(merged).end, interval.end)
    END FOR
    RETURN merged
END FUNCTION

title: Insert Interval
question: Insert a new interval into a sorted non-overlapping list and merge if necessary.
explanation: Iterate through the sorted intervals in three steps: push all intervals that end before the new interval starts, merge all overlapping intervals into the new interval, then push remaining intervals.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION insert(intervals, newInterval):
    res = [], i = 0, n = LENGTH(intervals)
    WHILE i < n AND intervals[i].end < newInterval.start DO:
        APPEND intervals[i] TO res; i = i + 1
    END WHILE
    WHILE i < n AND intervals[i].start <= newInterval.end DO:
        newInterval.start = MIN(newInterval.start, intervals[i].start)
        newInterval.end = MAX(newInterval.end, intervals[i].end)
        i = i + 1
    END WHILE
    APPEND newInterval TO res
    WHILE i < n DO APPEND intervals[i] TO res; i = i + 1
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Unique Paths
question: Find the number of unique paths from top-left to bottom-right in an m x n grid.
explanation: Since movement is restricted to moving down or right, the number of paths to reach cell (i, j) is the sum of paths to (i-1, j) and (i, j-1). We solve this dynamically using a 1D DP array.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION uniquePaths(m, n):
    row = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(n, INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
    FOR i FROM 1 TO m - 1 DO:
        newRow = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(n, INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
        FOR j FROM 1 TO n - 1 DO:
            newRow[j] = newRow[j - 1] + row[j]
        END FOR
        row = newRow
    END FOR
    RETURN row[n - 1]
END FUNCTION

title: Climbing Stairs
question: Count how many distinct ways you can climb n steps taking 1 or 2 steps at a time.
explanation: This follows the Fibonacci sequence pattern: the number of ways to reach step n is the sum of ways to reach step n-1 and step n-2. We track the last two results with O(1) memory.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION climbStairs(n):
    IF n <= 2 THEN RETURN n
    one = 1, two = 2
    FOR i FROM 3 TO n DO:
        temp = one + two
        one = two
        two = temp
    END FOR
    RETURN two
END FUNCTION

title: Edit Distance
question: Find minimum insertion, deletion, or replacement operations to convert word1 to word2.
explanation: We fill a 2D dynamic programming table where dp[i][j] represents the minimum ops to convert prefix word1[0..i] to word2[0..j]. If characters match, no action is needed; otherwise take 1 + min of insert, delete, replace.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION minDistance(word1, word2):
    m = LENGTH(word1), n = LENGTH(word2), dp = MATRIX(m + 1, n + 1, 0)
    FOR i FROM 0 TO m DO dp[i][0] = i
    FOR j FROM 0 TO n DO dp[0][j] = j
    FOR i FROM 1 TO m DO:
        FOR j FROM 1 TO n DO:
            IF word1[i-1] == word2[j-1] THEN dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]
            ELSE dp[i][j] = 1 + MIN(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN dp[m][n]
END FUNCTION

title: Search a 2D Matrix
question: Search for a target value in a row-and-column-sorted matrix.
explanation: Treat the m x n matrix as a single 1D flattened array of size m * n. Standard binary search is applied by translating index `mid` to matrix position `matrix[mid / n][mid % n]`.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION searchMatrix(matrix, target):
    m = LENGTH(matrix), n = LENGTH(matrix[0]), low = 0, high = m * n - 1
    WHILE low <= high DO:
        mid = (low + high) / 2
        val = matrix[mid / n][mid % n]
        IF val == target THEN RETURN True
        ELSE IF val < target THEN low = mid + 1
        ELSE high = mid - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION

title: Minimum Window Substring
question: Find the minimum substring in s that contains all characters of string t.
explanation: We use a sliding window. We expand the right pointer to include characters until all required frequency requirements for string t are satisfied, then contract the left pointer to find the minimal valid window size.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION minWindow(s, t):
    IF t IS EMPTY THEN RETURN ''
    countT = FREQ_MAP(t), window = EMPTY_MAP(), have = 0, need = LENGTH(countT)
    res = [-1, -1], resLen = INF, l = 0
    FOR r FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        c = s[r]; window[c] = window[c] + 1
        IF c IN countT AND window[c] == countT[c] THEN have = have + 1
        WHILE have == need DO:
            IF (r - l + 1) < resLen THEN res = [l, r]; resLen = r - l + 1
            window[s[l]] = window[s[l]] - 1
            IF s[l] IN countT AND window[s[l]] < countT[s[l]] THEN have = have - 1
            l = l + 1
        END WHILE
    END FOR
    RETURN resLen != INF ? SUBSTRING(s, res[0], res[1] + 1) : ''
END FUNCTION

title: Subsets
question: Return the power set (all subsets) of a set of unique elements.
explanation: At each element index during depth-first traversal, we branch into two choices: either include the current number in the subset or exclude it, yielding all 2^N total subsets.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION subsets(nums):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(i, curr):
        IF i == LENGTH(nums) THEN APPEND COPY(curr) TO res; RETURN
        APPEND nums[i] TO curr
        backtrack(i + 1, curr)
        POP curr
        backtrack(i + 1, curr)
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0, [])
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Word Search
question: Check if a target word exists by connecting adjacent letter cells in a 2D board.
explanation: Perform depth-first search from every cell matching the first letter of the target word. Recursively explore adjacent 4-directional cells, marking visited paths temporally to prevent duplicate character usage.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION exist(board, word):
    ROWS = LENGTH(board), COLS = LENGTH(board[0])
    FUNCTION dfs(r, c, i):
        IF i == LENGTH(word) THEN RETURN True
        IF r < 0 OR c < 0 OR r >= ROWS OR c >= COLS OR board[r][c] != word[i] THEN RETURN False
        temp = board[r][c]; board[r][c] = '#'
        found = dfs(r+1,c,i+1) OR dfs(r-1,c,i+1) OR dfs(r,c+1,i+1) OR dfs(r,c-1,i+1)
        board[r][c] = temp
        RETURN found
    END FUNCTION
    FOR r FROM 0 TO ROWS - 1 DO:
        FOR c FROM 0 TO COLS - 1 DO:
            IF dfs(r, c, 0) THEN RETURN True
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
question: Find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within a histogram.
explanation: We use a monotonic increasing stack storing bar indices. When encountering a shorter bar, we pop taller bars from the stack, calculating the area rectangle bounded by the height of each popped bar.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION largestRectangleArea(heights):
    stack = EMPTY_STACK(), maxArea = 0, n = LENGTH(heights)
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n DO:
        h = (i == n) ? 0 : heights[i]
        WHILE NOT IS_EMPTY(stack) AND heights[TOP(stack)] > h DO:
            height = heights[POP(stack)]
            width = IS_EMPTY(stack) ? i : i - TOP(stack) - 1
            maxArea = MAX(maxArea, height * width)
        END WHILE
        PUSH i TO stack
    END FOR
    RETURN maxArea
END FUNCTION

title: Decode Ways
question: Calculate the total number of ways to decode an encoded digit string to letters.
explanation: Using 1D dynamic programming, dp[i] represents decoding possibilities up to index i. Single-digit decodings (1-9) add dp[i-1], while double-digit combinations (10-26) add dp[i-2].
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION numDecodings(s):
    IF s[0] == '0' THEN RETURN 0
    dp = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(LENGTH(s) + 1, INITIAL_VALUE = 0)
    dp[0] = 1, dp[1] = 1
    FOR i FROM 2 TO LENGTH(s) DO:
        one = INT(SUBSTRING(s, i-1, i))
        two = INT(SUBSTRING(s, i-2, i))
        IF one >= 1 THEN dp[i] = dp[i] + dp[i-1]
        IF two >= 10 AND two <= 26 THEN dp[i] = dp[i] + dp[i-2]
    END FOR
    RETURN dp[LENGTH(s)]
END FUNCTION

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
question: Determine if a binary tree is a valid Binary Search Tree.
explanation: Recursively validate the tree by passing down allowable min and max boundary values for each node. Every node's value must strictly lie within its active (min, max) range.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isValidBST(root):
    FUNCTION validate(node, minVal, maxVal):
        IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN True
        IF node.val <= minVal OR node.val >= maxVal THEN RETURN False
        RETURN validate(node.left, minVal, node.val) AND validate(node.right, node.val, maxVal)
    END FUNCTION
    RETURN validate(root, -INFINITY, INFINITY)
END FUNCTION

title: Same Tree
question: Check if two binary trees are structurally identical with equal node values.
explanation: Traverse both trees simultaneously using depth-first search. At each node, check if both are NULL (true), one is NULL (false), or their values differ (false), then recurse left and right.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isSameTree(p, q):
    IF p IS NULL AND q IS NULL THEN RETURN True
    IF p IS NULL OR q IS NULL OR p.val != q.val THEN RETURN False
    RETURN isSameTree(p.left, q.left) AND isSameTree(p.right, q.right)
END FUNCTION

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
question: Traverse a binary tree level by level from left to right.
explanation: We use a queue to perform Breadth-First Search (BFS). In each iteration, we snapshot queue size to process all nodes belonging to the current level before moving to child nodes.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION levelOrder(root):
    IF root IS NULL THEN RETURN []
    queue = [root], res = []
    WHILE queue IS NOT EMPTY DO:
        levelSize = LENGTH(queue), currentLevel = []
        FOR i FROM 1 TO levelSize DO:
            node = DEQUEUE(queue)
            APPEND node.val TO currentLevel
            IF node.left THEN ENQUEUE(queue, node.left)
            IF node.right THEN ENQUEUE(queue, node.right)
        END FOR
        APPEND currentLevel TO res
    END WHILE
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
question: Find the maximum depth or path height from the root to the farthest leaf node.
explanation: Using depth-first search recursion, the maximum depth of a binary tree node is 1 + maximum depth among its left and right subtrees.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxDepth(root):
    IF root IS NULL THEN RETURN 0
    RETURN 1 + MAX(maxDepth(root.left), maxDepth(root.right))
END FUNCTION

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
question: Reconstruct a binary tree using its preorder and inorder traversal arrays.
explanation: The first element in the preorder traversal gives the root. Finding this value in the inorder traversal splits the tree into distinct left and right subtrees, allowing recursive reconstruction.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION buildTree(preorder, inorder):
    IF preorder IS EMPTY OR inorder IS EMPTY THEN RETURN NULL
    root = NEW Node(preorder[0])
    mid = INDEX_OF(inorder, preorder[0])
    root.left = buildTree(preorder[1 TO mid+1], inorder[0 TO mid])
    root.right = buildTree(preorder[mid+1 TO END], inorder[mid+1 TO END])
    RETURN root
END FUNCTION

title: Balanced Binary Tree
question: Check if the left and right subtrees of every node differ in height by at most 1.
explanation: Perform a bottom-up depth-first traversal returning height. If any subtree is unbalanced (height difference > 1), propagate -1 upward to short-circuit calculation to O(N) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isBalanced(root):
    FUNCTION checkHeight(node):
        IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN 0
        leftH = checkHeight(node.left)
        rightH = checkHeight(node.right)
        IF leftH == -1 OR rightH == -1 OR ABS(leftH - rightH) > 1 THEN RETURN -1
        RETURN 1 + MAX(leftH, rightH)
    END FUNCTION
    RETURN checkHeight(root) != -1
END FUNCTION

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
question: Maximize profit by choosing a single day to buy a stock and a future day to sell it.
explanation: Traverse prices keeping track of the minimum price observed so far. At each step, calculate potential profit if sold today and update the global maximum profit.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxProfit(prices):
    minPrice = INFINITY, maxProf = 0
    FOR price IN prices DO:
        IF price < minPrice THEN minPrice = price
        ELSE IF price - minPrice > maxProf THEN maxProf = price - minPrice
    END FOR
    RETURN maxProf
END FUNCTION

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
question: Find the maximum sum of any non-empty path between two nodes in a binary tree.
explanation: For each node, compute max gains from left and right children (ignoring negative gains). The maximum path centered at this node is node.val + leftGain + rightGain; update global max.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxPathSum(root):
    maxSum = -INFINITY
    FUNCTION getMaxGain(node):
        IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN 0
        leftGain = MAX(getMaxGain(node.left), 0)
        rightGain = MAX(getMaxGain(node.right), 0)
        maxSum = MAX(maxSum, node.val + leftGain + rightGain)
        RETURN node.val + MAX(leftGain, rightGain)
    END FUNCTION
    getMaxGain(root)
    RETURN maxSum
END FUNCTION

title: Valid Palindrome
question: Check if a string is a palindrome after converting to lowercase and removing non-alphanumeric characters.
explanation: Use two pointers starting at left and right boundaries. Skip non-alphanumeric characters and compare lowercase equivalents until pointers meet.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isPalindrome(s):
    l = 0, r = LENGTH(s) - 1
    WHILE l < r DO:
        WHILE l < r AND NOT IS_ALPHANUMERIC(s[l]) DO l = l + 1
        WHILE l < r AND NOT IS_ALPHANUMERIC(s[r]) DO r = r - 1
        IF LOWERCASE(s[l]) != LOWERCASE(s[r]) THEN RETURN False
        l = l + 1, r = r - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN True
END FUNCTION

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
question: Find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive numbers in an unsorted array.
explanation: Store elements in a Hash Set. Only start counting a consecutive sequence if `(num - 1)` is absent in the set, ensuring each number sequence is traversed only once in O(N) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION longestConsecutive(nums):
    numSet = SET(nums), longest = 0
    FOR num IN numSet DO:
        IF (num - 1) NOT IN numSet THEN:
            length = 1
            WHILE (num + length) IN numSet DO length = length + 1
            longest = MAX(longest, length)
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN longest
END FUNCTION

title: Clone Graph
question: Create a deep copy of a connected, undirected graph.
explanation: Use Depth First Search (DFS) along with a hash map mapping original nodes to cloned nodes. Clone original nodes on first visit and recursively attach cloned neighbor connections.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION cloneGraph(node):
    IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL
    visited = EMPTY_HASH_MAP()
    FUNCTION dfs(n):
        IF n IN visited THEN RETURN visited[n]
        copy = NEW Node(n.val)
        visited[n] = copy
        FOR neighbor IN n.neighbors DO:
            APPEND dfs(neighbor) TO copy.neighbors
        END FOR
        RETURN copy
    END FUNCTION
    RETURN dfs(node)
END FUNCTION

title: Copy List with Random Pointer
question: Deep copy a linked list where each node has a next pointer and a random pointer.
explanation: Pass 1: Traverse original list and populate a hash map mapping each original node to its new cloned node copy. Pass 2: Link the cloned nodes' `next` and `random` pointers using the hash map.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION copyRandomList(head):
    IF head IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL
    oldToNew = EMPTY_HASH_MAP(), curr = head
    WHILE curr IS NOT NULL DO:
        oldToNew[curr] = NEW Node(curr.val)
        curr = curr.next
    END WHILE
    curr = head
    WHILE curr IS NOT NULL DO:
        oldToNew[curr].next = oldToNew[curr.next]
        oldToNew[curr].random = oldToNew[curr.random]
        curr = curr.next
    END WHILE
    RETURN oldToNew[head]
END FUNCTION

title: Word Break
question: Determine if a string can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of dictionary words.
explanation: Work backward using a dynamic programming array dp[i] indicating whether substring s[i..n] can be segmented. If s[i..i+len] matches a dictionary word, set dp[i] = dp[i + len].
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION wordBreak(s, wordDict):
    dp = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(LENGTH(s) + 1, INITIAL_VALUE = False)
    dp[LENGTH(s)] = True
    FOR i FROM LENGTH(s) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
        FOR w IN wordDict DO:
            IF (i + LENGTH(w)) <= LENGTH(s) AND SUBSTRING(s, i, i + LENGTH(w)) == w THEN:
                dp[i] = dp[i + LENGTH(w)]
            IF dp[i] THEN BREAK
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN dp[0]
END FUNCTION

title: Linked List Cycle
question: Determine if a linked list contains a cycle using two pointer technique.
explanation: Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm uses two pointers moving at different speeds (slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps). If a cycle exists, the fast pointer will eventually overlap the slow pointer.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION hasCycle(head):
    slow = head, fast = head
    WHILE fast IS NOT NULL AND fast.next IS NOT NULL DO:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        IF slow == fast THEN RETURN True
    END WHILE
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION

title: Reorder List
question: Reorder a linked list to interleave nodes from the start and the end.
explanation: 1. Find middle node using fast/slow pointers. 2. Reverse second half of linked list in-place. 3. Merge first half and reversed second half alternately.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION reorderList(head):
    slow = head, fast = head.next
    WHILE fast AND fast.next DO slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next
    second = slow.next; slow.next = NULL; prev = NULL
    WHILE second DO temp = second.next; second.next = prev; prev = second; second = temp
    first = head; second = prev
    WHILE second DO
        t1 = first.next, t2 = second.next
        first.next = second; second.next = t1
        first = t1; second = t2
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

title: LRU Cache
question: Design a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with O(1) time operations.
explanation: Combine a Hash Map with a Doubly Linked List. Map stores keys pointing directly to list nodes for O(1) lookups, while list tracks usage ordering (MRU at head, LRU at tail).
pseudoCode:
CLASS LRUCache:
    CONSTRUCTOR(capacity):
        cap = capacity, cache = HASH_MAP(), left = Node(0,0), right = Node(0,0)
        left.next = right; right.prev = left
    FUNCTION get(key):
        IF key IN cache THEN REMOVE(cache[key]); INSERT(cache[key]); RETURN cache[key].val
        RETURN -1
    FUNCTION put(key, value):
        IF key IN cache THEN REMOVE(cache[key])
        cache[key] = NEW Node(key, value); INSERT(cache[key])
        IF LENGTH(cache) > cap THEN:
            lru = left.next; REMOVE(lru); DELETE cache[lru.key]
END CLASS

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
question: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression written in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix).
explanation: Push numbers onto stack. When an operator is encountered, pop two numbers, perform operation (second pop OP first pop), and push result back onto stack.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION evalRPN(tokens):
    stack = EMPTY_STACK()
    FOR t IN tokens DO:
        IF t IS OPERATOR THEN:
            b = POP(stack), a = POP(stack)
            PUSH APPLY_OP(a, b, t) TO stack
        ELSE PUSH INT(t) TO stack
    END FOR
    RETURN POP(stack)
END FUNCTION

title: Maximum Product Subarray
question: Find a contiguous non-empty subarray that has the largest product.
explanation: Track both running current max product and current min product (because multiplying two negative numbers creates a large positive product). Swap min/max whenever a negative number is encountered.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxProduct(nums):
    res = MAX(nums), curMin = 1, curMax = 1
    FOR n IN nums DO:
        temp = curMax * n
        curMax = MAX(n, temp, curMin * n)
        curMin = MIN(n, temp, curMin * n)
        res = MAX(res, curMax)
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
question: Find the minimum element in a sorted array that has been rotated.
explanation: Apply binary search: if mid element is greater than or equal to left element, pivot/minimum lies in right half; otherwise it lies in left half.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findMin(nums):
    l = 0, r = LENGTH(nums) - 1, res = nums[0]
    WHILE l <= r DO:
        IF nums[l] < nums[r] THEN res = MIN(res, nums[l]); BREAK
        m = (l + r) / 2
        res = MIN(res, nums[m])
        IF nums[m] >= nums[l] THEN l = m + 1
        ELSE r = m - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Min Stack
question: Design a stack that retrieves the minimum element in O(1) time.
explanation: Maintain an auxiliary minStack parallel to the main stack. At each push step, append min(val, top of minStack) onto minStack so current minimum is always stored at top.
pseudoCode:
CLASS MinStack:
    CONSTRUCTOR(): stack = [], minStack = []
    FUNCTION push(val):
        PUSH val TO stack
        val = MIN(val, IS_EMPTY(minStack) ? val : TOP(minStack))
        PUSH val TO minStack
    FUNCTION pop(): POP stack; POP minStack
    FUNCTION top(): RETURN TOP(stack)
    FUNCTION getMin(): RETURN TOP(minStack)
END CLASS

title: House Robber
question: Maximize total stolen amount along a row of houses without robbing two adjacent ones.
explanation: At house i, maximum profit is max(nums[i] + rob1, rob2), where rob1 is max profit 2 houses back and rob2 is max profit 1 house back.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION rob(nums):
    rob1 = 0, rob2 = 0
    FOR n IN nums DO:
        temp = MAX(n + rob1, rob2)
        rob1 = rob2
        rob2 = temp
    END FOR
    RETURN rob2
END FUNCTION

title: Number of Islands
question: Count the number of 4-directionally connected land islands in a 2D grid.
explanation: Iterate through matrix. When seeing '1', increment island count and fire BFS/DFS to sink all connected land ('1' -> '0') to prevent double counting.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION numIslands(grid):
    IF grid IS EMPTY THEN RETURN 0
    count = 0, ROWS = LENGTH(grid), COLS = LENGTH(grid[0])
    FUNCTION dfs(r, c):
        IF r < 0 OR c < 0 OR r >= ROWS OR c >= COLS OR grid[r][c] == '0' THEN RETURN
        grid[r][c] = '0'
        dfs(r+1, c); dfs(r-1, c); dfs(r, c+1); dfs(r, c-1)
    END FUNCTION
    FOR r FROM 0 TO ROWS - 1 DO:
        FOR c FROM 0 TO COLS - 1 DO:
            IF grid[r][c] == '1' THEN count = count + 1; dfs(r, c)
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN count
END FUNCTION

title: Reverse Linked List
question: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively or recursively.
explanation: Maintain `prev` (NULL) and `curr` (head). Save `curr.next`, redirect `curr.next = prev`, shift `prev = curr` and `curr = next` until traversal finishes.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION reverseList(head):
    prev = NULL, curr = head
    WHILE curr IS NOT NULL DO:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    END WHILE
    RETURN prev
END FUNCTION

title: Course Schedule
question: Determine if it is possible to finish all courses given their prerequisite dependencies.
explanation: Detect cycle in directed graph using DFS or Kahn's topological sort (BFS in-degree). If a cycle exists, completing all courses is impossible.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION canFinish(numCourses, prerequisites):
    preMap = HASH_MAP_OF_LISTS(), visited = SET()
    FOR req IN prerequisites DO APPEND req[1] TO preMap[req[0]]
    FUNCTION dfs(crs):
        IF crs IN visited THEN RETURN False
        IF preMap[crs] IS EMPTY THEN RETURN True
        ADD crs TO visited
        FOR pre IN preMap[crs] DO:
            IF NOT dfs(pre) THEN RETURN False
        END FOR
        REMOVE crs FROM visited; preMap[crs] = []
        RETURN True
    END FUNCTION
    FOR c FROM 0 TO numCourses - 1 DO:
        IF NOT dfs(c) THEN RETURN False
    END FOR
    RETURN True
END FUNCTION

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
question: Implement a trie supporting insert, search, and startsWith methods.
explanation: A tree where each node represents a character mapping to nested dynamic children objects and an `isWord` boolean flag marking full word completions.
pseudoCode:
CLASS Trie:
    CONSTRUCTOR(): root = NEW TrieNode()
    FUNCTION insert(word):
        curr = root
        FOR c IN word DO:
            IF c NOT IN curr.children THEN curr.children[c] = NEW TrieNode()
            curr = curr.children[c]
        END FOR
        curr.isWord = True
    FUNCTION search(word):
        node = findNode(word)
        RETURN node IS NOT NULL AND node.isWord
    FUNCTION startsWith(prefix):
        RETURN findNode(prefix) IS NOT NULL
END CLASS

title: Course Schedule II
question: Return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all prerequisite courses.
explanation: Perform Topological Sort via BFS (Kahn's Algorithm). Track in-degree count of each course node; process nodes with 0 in-degree and reduce dependencies of adjacent nodes.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findOrder(numCourses, prerequisites):
    adj = HASH_MAP_OF_LISTS(), inDegree = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(numCourses, 0)
    FOR p IN prerequisites DO APPEND p[0] TO adj[p[1]]; inDegree[p[0]] = inDegree[p[0]] + 1
    queue = [c FOR c IN 0..numCourses-1 IF inDegree[c] == 0], res = []
    WHILE queue IS NOT EMPTY DO:
        c = DEQUEUE(queue); APPEND c TO res
        FOR nxt IN adj[c] DO:
            inDegree[nxt] = inDegree[nxt] - 1
            IF inDegree[nxt] == 0 THEN ENQUEUE(queue, nxt)
        END FOR
    END WHILE
    RETURN LENGTH(res) == numCourses ? res : []
END FUNCTION

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
question: Build a structure that supports adding words and searching with wildcard dots.
explanation: Store words in Trie. For normal characters traverse children directly. For wildcard '.' character, recursively check all child branches at current node level.
pseudoCode:
CLASS WordDictionary:
    CONSTRUCTOR(): root = NEW TrieNode()
    FUNCTION addWord(word):
        curr = root
        FOR c IN word DO:
            IF c NOT IN curr.children THEN curr.children[c] = NEW TrieNode()
            curr = curr.children[c]
        END FOR
        curr.isWord = True
    FUNCTION search(word):
        FUNCTION dfs(j, root):
            curr = root
            FOR i FROM j TO LENGTH(word) - 1 DO:
                c = word[i]
                IF c == '.' THEN:
                    FOR child IN curr.children.values() DO:
                        IF dfs(i + 1, child) THEN RETURN True
                    END FOR
                    RETURN False
                ELSE:
                    IF c NOT IN curr.children THEN RETURN False
                    curr = curr.children[c]
            END FOR
            RETURN curr.isWord
        END FUNCTION
        RETURN dfs(0, root)
END CLASS

title: Word Search II
question: Find all dictionary words that can be constructed on a 2D character board.
explanation: Insert target words into a Trie structure. Run DFS from each board cell, stepping through both the 2D grid and matching Trie nodes concurrently to prune invalid search paths.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findWords(board, words):
    trie = BUILD_TRIE(words), res = SET(), visited = SET()
    ROWS = LENGTH(board), COLS = LENGTH(board[0])
    FUNCTION dfs(r, c, node, word):
        IF r < 0 OR c < 0 OR r >= ROWS OR c >= COLS OR (r,c) IN visited OR board[r][c] NOT IN node.children THEN RETURN
        ADD (r,c) TO visited; node = node.children[board[r][c]]; word = word + board[r][c]
        IF node.isWord THEN ADD word TO res
        dfs(r+1,c,node,word); dfs(r-1,c,node,word); dfs(r,c+1,node,word); dfs(r,c-1,node,word)
        REMOVE (r,c) FROM visited
    END FUNCTION
    FOR r FROM 0 TO ROWS - 1 DO:
        FOR c FROM 0 TO COLS - 1 DO dfs(r, c, trie.root, '')
    END FOR
    RETURN ARRAY(res)
END FUNCTION

title: House Robber II
question: Maximize stolen amount in a circular arrangement of houses where first and last are connected.
explanation: Since house 1 and house N are adjacent, run standard House Robber twice: once on subarray range [0..N-2] and once on range [1..N-1], returning max of both results.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION rob(nums):
    IF LENGTH(nums) == 1 THEN RETURN nums[0]
    RETURN MAX(robRange(nums, 0, LENGTH(nums)-2), robRange(nums, 1, LENGTH(nums)-1))
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION robRange(nums, start, end):
    r1 = 0, r2 = 0
    FOR i FROM start TO end DO:
        temp = MAX(nums[i] + r1, r2); r1 = r2; r2 = temp
    END FOR
    RETURN r2
END FUNCTION

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
question: Find the kth largest element in an unsorted array without sorting completely.
explanation: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. Push elements into heap; whenever heap size exceeds k, pop minimum element. Root of heap will hold kth largest element in O(N log k) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findKthLargest(nums, k):
    minHeap = NEW MinHeap()
    FOR num IN nums DO:
        minHeap.PUSH(num)
        IF minHeap.SIZE() > k THEN minHeap.POP()
    END FOR
    RETURN minHeap.TOP()
END FUNCTION

title: Contains Duplicate
question: Check if any value appears at least twice in an integer array.
explanation: Iterate through array while adding numbers to a Hash Set. If current number is already present in set, immediately return True.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION containsDuplicate(nums):
    seen = EMPTY_SET()
    FOR n IN nums DO:
        IF n IN seen THEN RETURN True
        ADD n TO seen
    END FOR
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION

title: Invert Binary Tree
question: Invert a binary tree so that left and right children are swapped recursively.
explanation: Recursively swap the left and right subtrees for every node in the tree.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION invertTree(root):
    IF root IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL
    temp = root.left
    root.left = invertTree(root.right)
    root.right = invertTree(temp)
    RETURN root
END FUNCTION

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
question: Find the kth smallest value in a Binary Search Tree using inorder property.
explanation: In-order traversal of BST yields nodes in strictly sorted ascending order. Perform iterative in-order traversal using stack and return the kth visited element.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION kthSmallest(root, k):
    stack = EMPTY_STACK(), curr = root, n = 0
    WHILE curr IS NOT NULL OR NOT IS_EMPTY(stack) DO:
        WHILE curr IS NOT NULL DO PUSH curr TO stack; curr = curr.left
        curr = POP(stack); n = n + 1
        IF n == k THEN RETURN curr.val
        curr = curr.right
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
question: Find the lowest common ancestor node of two given nodes in a BST.
explanation: Traverse BST starting at root: if both p and q values are larger than curr.val, move right; if both are smaller, move left; otherwise current node is split point / LCA.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION lowestCommonAncestor(root, p, q):
    curr = root
    WHILE curr DO:
        IF p.val > curr.val AND q.val > curr.val THEN curr = curr.right
        ELSE IF p.val < curr.val AND q.val < curr.val THEN curr = curr.left
        ELSE RETURN curr
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

title: Product of Array Except Self
question: Construct an output array where each index equals the product of all array elements except itself.
explanation: Build prefix products array left to right, then multiply each position by running postfix product from right to left in O(N) time without using division.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION productExceptSelf(nums):
    res = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(LENGTH(nums), INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
    prefix = 1
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        res[i] = prefix; prefix = prefix * nums[i]
    END FOR
    postfix = 1
    FOR i FROM LENGTH(nums) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
        res[i] = res[i] * postfix; postfix = postfix * nums[i]
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION

title: Sliding Window Maximum
question: Find the maximum element within every sliding window of size k moving across an array.
explanation: Maintain a monotonic decreasing Deque storing indices. Deque front always stores maximum index for active window of size k in O(N) time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxSlidingWindow(nums, k):
    output = [], q = NEW Deque(), l = 0
    FOR r FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        WHILE NOT IS_EMPTY(q) AND nums[LAST(q)] < nums[r] DO POP_BACK(q)

        END IF
    END FOR

END FUNCTION

title: Missing Number
question: Find the single missing number in an array containing n distinct numbers in range [0, n].
explanation: Use bitwise XOR operation across all numbers from 0 to N and all values present in array. Equal matching numbers negate out via `x ^ x = 0`, leaving only missing number.

title: Find Median from Data Stream

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree

title: Coin Change
question: Calculate the fewest coins needed to make up a target amount of money.
explanation: Build 1D dynamic array `dp` from 0 up to target `amount`. For each amount x, iterate through available coins `c` to calculate min transition: `dp[x] = min(dp[x], 1 + dp[x - c])`.

FUNCTION coinChange(coins, amount):

    FOR a FROM 1 TO amount DO:

            IF a - c >= 0 THEN dp[a] = MIN(dp[a], 1 + dp[a - c])

END FUNCTION

title: Counting Bits

title: Sum of Two Integers
question: Calculate the sum of two integers without using + or - operators.
explanation: Bitwise XOR `a ^ b` computes addition without carry bits, while Bitwise AND shifted left `(a & b) << 1` computes carry bits. Repeat until carry equals 0.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow

FUNCTION pacificAtlantic(heights):

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement

title: Redundant Connection
question: Find an edge that can be removed to turn a graph back into an unrooted tree.
explanation: Use Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union). Iterate through edges: if both vertices share same parent representative, this edge creates cycle and is returned as redundant.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findRedundantConnection(edges):
    parent = [i FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(edges)]
    FUNCTION find(n):
        p = parent[n]
        WHILE p != parent[p] DO parent[p] = parent[parent[p]]; p = parent[p]
        RETURN p
    END FUNCTION
    FUNCTION union(n1, n2):
        p1, p2 = find(n1), find(n2)
        IF p1 == p2 THEN RETURN False
        parent[p1] = p2; RETURN True
    END FUNCTION
    FOR n1, n2 IN edges DO:
        IF NOT union(n1, n2) THEN RETURN [n1, n2]
    END FOR
END FUNCTION

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops

title: Rotting Oranges

FUNCTION orangesRotting(grid):

END FUNCTION

title: Longest Common Subsequence

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points

    FOR i FROM 0 TO N - 1 DO:
        FOR j FROM i + 1 TO N - 1 DO:
            dist = ABS(points[i][0] - points[j][0]) + ABS(points[i][1] - points[j][1])
            APPEND [dist, j] TO adj[i]; APPEND [dist, i] TO adj[j]
        END FOR
    END FOR
    res = 0, visit = SET(), minHeap = MinHeap([[0, 0]])
    WHILE LENGTH(visit) < N DO:
        [cost, i] = POP(minHeap)
        IF i IN visit THEN CONTINUE
        res = res + cost; ADD i TO visit
        FOR neiCost, nei IN adj[i] DO:
            IF nei NOT IN visit THEN PUSH [neiCost, nei] TO minHeap
        END FOR
    END WHILE
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
